clue.text: Grounds for growing concern

parts.note: read as worrying reasons for anxiety that keeps increasing, but really land on which crops are grown by a business

explanation.surface: Something gives reason for mounting worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like worry, but here it means a business, and 'grounds' are literal fields where crops are grown.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultivated holding is a business (a concern) whose fields are used for raising crops.

clue.text: Performed in a group or in solitary state

indicators.note: in says the word for performed goes inside the group

parts.note: a band is a musical group, with A kept
something performed has been done

explanation.surface: Something was done either with others or all alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DONE inside A BAND, splitting it as A BAN-DONE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left deserted is alone, in a solitary condition.

clue.text: Keeps in the French capital

indicators.note: in says the word for keeps sits inside the French article

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
to keep something is to have it, so keeps gives has

explanation.surface: Something is stored in the capital of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'French capital' to be Paris, but 'the French' is LA and 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Tibet.

clue.text: Note smart appearance restricting food-intake

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: A note about someone's smart look while they are on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' gives no letters and acts only as a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without meals is limiting what you eat.

clue.text: A roll filled with nothing but chicken

indicators.note: filled with says the word for roll has the zero placed inside it

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bread roll with only chicken as filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' suggests bread, but it is a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A male domestic fowl is a type of chicken.

clue.text: Finding a way around company tax

indicators.note: around says the abbreviation for way goes round the one for company

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a method of dodging corporation tax.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT is an old word for a levy, as in 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot is an archaic word for a levy or payment, surviving in 'scot-free'.

clue.text: Figure on a Shakespearean role, that's plain

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a figure
Lear is the title role of King Lear

explanation.surface: A figure placed on a Shakespeare part makes things obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets C above LEAR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and obvious things are easy to understand.

clue.text: Makes an inventory, like the neat thief

definitions.meaning: a shop counting its goods is assessing its holdings
neat is an old word for cattle, so a cattle rustler literally removes livestock

explanation.surface: Counting goods, as a tidy burglar might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy' but is an old word for cattle, and 'stock' can mean livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting goods is a review of holdings; a cattle thief removes livestock.

clue.text: Needlewoman is without credit, she'll give voice

indicators.note: is without here means is outside, so the sewer's word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a seamer is one who sews seams

explanation.surface: A seamstress has no credit and will speak up about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside' in this old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who yells and shrieks is giving voice loudly.

clue.text: An American lawyer holding drive is for show

indicators.note: holding says the lawyer's letters hold the word for drive

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor
to ram is to drive forcefully

explanation.surface: A US attorney with drive is just showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A play performed on stage is a show.

clue.text: Rash investigation?

parts.note: read as a hasty inquiry, but also a look at spots on the skin from a rash

explanation.surface: A hasty, ill-considered inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like 'hasty', but here it is a skin eruption made of spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A random sudden inspection is a quick test; punningly, examining spots.

clue.text: The visionary's idle — it's a failing

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters break down and are put together anew

parts.note: the words it's a, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Being idle is the dreamer's weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' signals an anagram of IDLE + ITSA (from "it's a"); 's in the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer with lofty principles is a visionary.

clue.text: Investing money in sound equipment for Lords

indicators.note: investing in means placing the money inside the hearing organs
in completes 'investing in', placing the letter for money inside

parts.note: ears are the organs of hearing
L stands for pound (libra), money

explanation.surface: Peers put their money into hi-fi gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound equipment' suggests stereo gear but means the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers of a rank below marquess are members of the House of Lords.

clue.text: He wrote Rock-face Untamed in Old English

indicators.note: in says the two words go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff
untamed means wild

explanation.surface: An author's book title 'Rock-face Untamed' written in Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a book title, but 'He wrote' is the definition and 'in' wraps the abbreviation for Old English round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright was a writer of plays and stories.

clue.text: Small and secure means of defence

parts.note: to bag something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A compact and safe way to defend yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled sacks are stacked to protect against floods or gunfire.

clue.text: Providing a bag ends the need for wrappings

indicators.note: providing, in the sense of making or fashioning, signals the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A bag removes the need for wrapping paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providing' looks like 'if', but works as the anagram indicator on A BAG ENDS; 'the need for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of cloth bound round wounds are dressings or wrappings.

clue.text: Go on about a member standing up

indicators.note: about says the rant goes round the other letters

parts.note: to go on at length is to rant
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Ranting at length about an MP who rose to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry a rampant beast is rearing up on its hind legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a rampant animal is rearing upright on its hind legs.

clue.text: A high-flier requires space to manoeuvre

definitions.text: A high-flier requires space to manoeuvre

parts.words: A high-flier requires space to manoeuvre
parts.note: read as an ambitious person needing elbow room, but really someone who flies and manoeuvres in outer space

explanation.surface: An ambitious person needs room to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a career achiever, and 'space' elbow room; both are literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacefarer flies very high and works in outer space.

clue.text: Some eland antelope are rather slow

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some antelopes are not very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning moderately slow, at walking pace.

clue.text: The movement away from the land

definitions.text: The movement away from the land

parts.words: The movement away from the land
parts.note: read as rural depopulation, people leaving farms, but really sea water receding from the shore

explanation.surface: People leaving the countryside for towns.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rural people migrating to cities; it is the sea going out.
explanation.definitionFit: The outgoing flow of the sea recedes from the shore.

clue.text: Jerk after rare settlement would be irregular

indicators.note: after places the twitch at the end
settlement suggests the letters are resettled in a new order

parts.note: a tic is a twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A sudden twitch following an unusual settlement looks odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' rearranges the letters of 'rare' to ERRA, and 'after' sets the twitch at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpredictable and uneven is irregular.

clue.text: Old flame alluded to as on edge

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
something cited is referred to

explanation.surface: A former lover mentioned makes someone nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated and keyed up is being on edge.

clue.text: Stick by a girl

parts.note: a wand is a thin stick

explanation.surface: Stay loyal to a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name.

clue.text: Verne's odd courage

indicators.note: odd signals the name's letters are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Jules Verne's peculiar bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the letters of VERNE; the 's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldness and daring is courage.

clue.text: Missiles costing no more than one dollar?

definitions.text: Missiles costing no more than one dollar?

parts.words: Missiles costing no more than one dollar?
parts.note: a buck is a dollar, so cheap shot could be called a dollar's worth of pellets

explanation.surface: Cheap ammunition sold for a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCK is US slang for a dollar, so the whimsical reading is shot priced at a buck.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse lead pellets fired from a shotgun are missiles.

clue.text: Brown's got a Greek character in deep water

indicators.note: in says the letter goes into the water

parts.note: the sea is deep water
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown has a Greek in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname; it is the colour, and 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown pigment, originally from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Some private arrangement made about rent

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A private deal was struck concerning the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'made about rent' as definition; only 'rent' (a rip) defines, and 'made about' is a link. 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip in fabric is a rent.

clue.text: A criminal's alternative isn't clear

indicators.note: alternative suggests another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A crook's other option is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges ISNT + CLEAR; the 's in the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who commits theft is a criminal.

clue.text: Smooth modern form of transport

definitions.meaning: to smooth wood with a tool is to level it
an aircraft, a twentieth-century way to travel

explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's tool smooths wood; an aircraft is a modern means of travel.

clue.text: The viewers have a point, certainly

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
yes means certainly

explanation.surface: Spectators make a valid argument, without doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' suggests audience; it is the organs of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are what see things, our viewers.

clue.text: Dream as the acting top man

indicators.note: acting suggests the letters perform a new role, rearranged

explanation.surface: An imaginary acting head of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal of a school is its top man.
